nuclear-power-reactor.alt: A nuclear power plant. In the reactor, green fuel rods of uranium-235 stand between dark control rods. Hot water flows to a steam generator; steam spins a turbine connected to a generator that sends out electricity. Used steam goes to a condenser cooled by a cooling tower, and cooler water returns to the reactor. Notes say control rods absorb neutrons to slow or stop the chain reaction, and that in fission a neutron splits U-235, releasing heat and 2 or 3 more neutrons.
